title: MCP Ecosystem 2026
content:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) was released by Anthropic in November 2024 as an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources. By mid-2026, it has grown from a promising specification into the dominant integration layer for AI agents, with over 500 public servers and a new specification release candidate that addresses enterprise-scale deployment.

---

## Server Ecosystem Scale

As of Q2 2026, the public MCP server count exceeds 500, with new servers added weekly by community contributors, SaaS vendors, and enterprise teams. Major categories include:

| Category | Example Servers |
|---|---|
| Databases | PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB |
| File storage | Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, S3 |
| Developer tools | GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Asana |
| Communication | Slack, Gmail, Discord |
| Web | Brave Search, Puppeteer, Playwright, Firecrawl |
| Cloud infra | AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker |
| Data & analytics | Stripe, Airtable, Notion, Snowflake |
| Observability | Datadog, Sentry, PagerDuty |

The canonical reference list is maintained at `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers`.

---

## 2026 Specification Release Candidate

The MCP working group published a release candidate for the next spec revision with a final target date of July 28, 2026. Key changes:

### Stateless Protocol Core
The core protocol is redesigned around stateless request-response semantics. This eliminates the mismatch between MCP's previous stateful session model and typical HTTP load balancers, making horizontal scaling straightforward.

### Extensions Framework
A formalized mechanism for servers to advertise optional capabilities. Clients can inspect what extensions a server supports before connecting, enabling capability-based routing without out-of-band documentation.

### Tasks
First-class support for long-running asynchronous tasks. A client can initiate a task, receive a task ID, and poll or subscribe for completion — rather than blocking a single request for the duration.

### MCP Apps
A new primitive that bundles a server, a default prompt, and a UI schema into a single distributable unit. Designed to make it easy to publish end-user-facing agents through app stores or internal catalogs.

### Authorization Hardening
Standardized OAuth 2.1 flows replace the previous ad-hoc token-passing conventions. SSO-integrated auth is now part of the spec rather than a vendor extension.

### Formal Deprecation Policy
The spec now includes a versioned deprecation policy with 12-month notice requirements, addressing a pain point for enterprise adopters who need stability guarantees.

---

## Enterprise Deployment Challenges

Running MCP at scale has surfaced a consistent set of infrastructure gaps:

- **Session stickiness:** The pre-2026-RC stateful session model requires sticky routing or external session stores when running multiple server replicas behind a load balancer.
- **Audit trails:** Standard MCP has no built-in logging of tool calls. Enterprise deployments add a gateway layer that records every call, input, and output for compliance.
- **Configuration portability:** Each MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, custom apps) uses its own config format for listing servers. There is no cross-client standard, though the Extensions framework in the 2026 RC addresses discovery.
- **Discovery without connection:** Crawlers and registries cannot inspect a server's capabilities without establishing a live session. The Extensions RC adds a static manifest endpoint to fix this.

---

## Transport Landscape

| Transport | Use case |
|---|---|
| `stdio` | Local servers co-located with the client (most common for CLI tools) |
| `http+sse` | Remote servers; event stream for server-to-client push |
| `websocket` | Lower-latency bidirectional; less common but growing |

The 2026 RC deprecates the older SSE framing in favor of a cleaner HTTP streaming model compatible with standard reverse proxies.

---

## Building an MCP Server (Quick Reference)

```typescript
import { Server } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js";
import { StdioServerTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js";

const server = new Server({ name: "my-server", version: "1.0.0" }, {
  capabilities: { tools: {} }
});

server.setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, async () => ({
  tools: [{ name: "my_tool", description: "...", inputSchema: { ... } }]
}));

server.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, async (req) => {
  // handle tool call
});

await server.connect(new StdioServerTransport());
```

The TypeScript SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) and Python SDK (`mcp`) are the two official implementations. The community maintains Go, Rust, and Java ports.
